Hi Samira — thanks for the clear set of questions. Below is a concise, shareable summary you can use with procurement/security, followed by a few technical notes.

Short, shareable statement:
"By default, Redwood's hosted API may retain full prompt and output payloads for up to 30 days for abuse detection, troubleshooting, and model quality monitoring. Request metadata (timestamps, non-sensitive headers, and basic usage metrics) may be retained longer per customer contract. Customers requiring zero retention of payload data can choose Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private deployments. In Dedicated/Private configurations, you'll get per-customer isolation, optional disabling of payload logging, the ability to configure retention windows, and support for customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM). Data residency controls (US, EU regions) are available in Dedicated and Private deployments."

Technical clarifications and notes:
- Hosted (default):
  • Payload retention: up to 30 days (configurable in enterprise contracts); used for abuse detection, debugging, and quality monitoring.
  • Logs: request metadata retained by region based on contract; not cross-customer merged; retention default is 90 days but can be adjusted under enterprise agreements.
  • Encryption: data encrypted at rest and in transit with Redwood-managed keys by default.

- Redwood Dedicated / Private:
  • Option to disable payload storage entirely (no prompts/outputs written to long-term stores).
  • All logs and storage can be routed to your VPC/S3 endpoints (customer-managed storage) when using Private deployment.
  • Support for customer-managed KMS/HSM for both Dedicated and Private.
  • Data residency: choose region(s) for storage and logging (US-only available).

- Implementation notes:
  • KV caches used for latency may be stored in memory and not persisted unless configured; persistent caches are optional and under customer control for Dedicated/Private.
  • Streaming and function-calling are supported in Dedicated/Private; disabling payload logging may affect debugability but not core runtime features.
  • Access controls: role-based access, audit logs for operator access, and IP allowlists are standard for Dedicated/Private.

Attachments included: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf, pii-data-flow-diagram.png
